title: TOTAL WRITE-OFF
summary: Players left and investors found no elegant way to call that engagement.

title: QUIET FAILURE
summary: The product harmed the audience and barely helped the business.

title: EXTRACTIVE DRIFT
summary: The business survived by spending player goodwill it did not have.

title: HOSTILE SUCCESS
summary: The numbers worked, provided nobody asked what happened to the players.

title: WHALE FARM
summary: The audience collapsed into a payment funnel with excellent quarterly posture.

title: FAILED SOFT LAUNCH
summary: Players were unhappy and the business case stayed imaginary.

title: MANAGED DECLINE
summary: Every constituency received a smaller disappointment than expected.

title: RETENTION THEATER
summary: The game kept enough dashboards alive to disguise how little anyone enjoyed it.

title: MONETIZED RESENTMENT
summary: The product made money from players who increasingly sounded like witnesses.

title: EXCELLENTLY HATED
summary: Investors applauded the machine while the community searched for the emergency exit.

title: BELOVED BUT BROKE
summary: Enough players cared to mourn the business model properly.

title: COMMUNITY PATCH
summary: The game had defenders, which was fortunate because revenue did not volunteer.

title: STRATEGIC AMBIGUITY
summary: Nobody was happy enough to celebrate or angry enough to simplify the meeting.

title: SUSTAINABLE ENOUGH
summary: The product found a profitable compromise and dared everyone to call it design.

title: OPTIMIZED COMPROMISE
summary: The numbers looked wonderful if the players were kept out of the slide deck.

title: CULT CLASSIC
summary: Players loved it with the financial intensity of a handwritten thank-you note.

title: GOOD GAME, BAD BUSINESS
summary: The update path created real affection and very few reasons for finance to smile.

title: RESPECTABLE MIRACLE
summary: The game became good enough that the business had to pretend this was planned.

title: ACTUAL PRODUCT MARKET FIT
summary: For one dangerous moment, progress served both the audience and the spreadsheet.

title: GOLDEN PATCH CYCLE
summary: Players stayed, money moved, and leadership became briefly insufferable.

title: ARTISTIC BANKRUPTCY
summary: The game became beautiful in precisely the way creditors dislike.

title: PLAYER SANCTUARY
summary: The community found a home and the business found a polite way to panic.

title: GOODWILL ENGINE
summary: Players trusted the game enough to keep it alive while revenue tried to catch up.

title: RARE ALIGNMENT
summary: The product respected players and still found money on purpose.

title: IMPOSSIBLY HEALTHY
summary: The game made everyone happy, creating suspicion among experienced producers.
